finding: Roles template (SOP-001-A04) has no builder or assembler role, though G0 asks who builds and G2 cites the chosen assembler
Plan template (SOP-004-A01) has no field for open items, problem and users, or iteration ECRs
SOP-004 and gates.yaml say CI blocks gates, but the template ships no CI; a file-exists check would pass a blank template
SOP-004 appendix table says A06 is not copied, but forms/SOP-004-A06-gate-checklists.md is in product repos
Pilot runs under draft procedures at a commit, not a release tag
No defined place for a G0 record: G0 is approval-only but AGENTS.md asks for a review package; A01/A02 gate field lists only G1 to G4
Commit prefix conventions conflict: [PN]/[DOC] in AGENTS.md, [LSN] used by the session, [QMS] in the template's first commit
SOP-001 §8 says approve after a break, ideally next day; same-day gates pull the other way
Procedures don't say whether a human-named platform at G0 is allowed or belongs in G1
No defined place to archive the G0 approval transcript; raw transcripts hold personal data that AGENTS.md rule 7 keeps out of repos
Unclear whether independent review is required when the agent authors and the human approves
G0 and G1 are split too finely for a small product; consider one combined review for simple products
Agent pulled design detail into G0; the G0 checklist doesn't limit how deep G0 goes
Reviews in a commentable document are not covered by SOP-003, which expects package.md in the repo
PR template (SOP-001-A02) only fits part changes; gate records and plans need a plain template
AGENTS.md says ask the gate's questions; agent opened with preset questions. Start each gate with a read-back and open conversation, as a per-user preference

Review burden too high for a small product: G0 and G1 each took more than one session. Agent should pre-fill recommendations, show at most five material findings, and keep QMS findings out of product reviews
A03 has no field for standards or accepted/proposed status, and no ID scheme for inspection or review verification; A04 doesn't define a serious risk or residual rating

ECRs take GitHub issue numbers, which are shared with PRs, so the first ECR was #3. kc wants a per-project ECR register (ECR-001, ECR-002 ...) with its own sequence; SOP-001, the ECR template and the commit format in AGENTS.md should cite that ID. This repo now keeps 00_planning/ecrs.csv
The ECR issue template applies an ECR label that the product template never creates

No path for parts taken from existing inventory: trace.csv needs a purchase line and CI checks it, but inventory parts have no order. Suggest an inventory purchase line (source, date found, original supplier if known) plus normal incoming inspection

No approved-alternates mechanism: SOP-002 says a non-drop-in replacement MPN gets a new PN but not who decides a drop-in substitute or how it is recorded. kc: a human declares a 1-for-1 swap. Suggest an approved alternates list per PN

kc expected LSN-0001 for the first custom part; SOP-002 §3 and new_pn.py share one number sequence between parts and assemblies, so LSN-A-0001 used number 1. Decide whether parts and assemblies get separate sequences
Product repo AGENTS.md does not point agents to the playbook skills (fusion-cad etc.), so the agent modelled the housing without reading fusion-cad first

No rigour levels: a lab pilot carries the same records as a regulated product. kc: wants it 'close to research/hobby level where the scope/design requirements/test stuff is all kind of taken care of itself after understanding through conversation'. Suggest a rigour level set at G0 (pilot / lab tool / regulated) that scales the records each gate needs, with agents drafting documents from the conversation in one pass

No per-unit build sign-off: build.yaml (SOP-006-A01) names one builder per build and lists serials, but has no per-unit record of who assembled it, when, and that the final checks passed; release.yaml (SOP-007-A04) is the only sign-off. kc expects an assembler sign-off after each build. Suggest per-unit fields in build.yaml units (sn, assembled_by, date, final_checks)

A requirement's source credited kc for ranges the agent proposed and kc accepted by default (REQ-006: 15 to 35 °C, 20 to 80 %RH). SOP-004 and the requirements template should tell 'stated by a person' from 'proposed by an agent, accepted by default', since defaults accepted in bulk are easy to mistake later for the user's own numbers

kc: the design output should be one controlled document with a PN and rev (the assembly instruction), with appendices: A BOM, B make files (STEP/STL/drawings zip, Gerbers), C inspection and test, D build traveller. minimalQMS instead spreads it over parts.csv, bom.csv, inspection_checks.csv and test_procedures/ with no document rev. LSN now generates LSN-A-0001_revA.pdf from those sources. Suggest SOP-004/SOP-006 define the build document and its appendices; data files become sources only

kc: the BOM must be readable and orderable: one BOM per assembly (no parent_pn column), category Custom (part) / Custom (assembly) / OTS, rev for every custom PN, units in capitals (EA), Ref spelled out as the assembly-instruction callout, and supplier, SKU, manufacturer, MPN, link and price for OTS parts. Suggest SOP-002-A02 adopt these columns; ordering data is duplicated per project (the OTS library is likely personal)

kc: inspection checks are hard to read as CSV and must be written for the inspector; incoming inspection, in-process checks and post-process tests need telling apart, and the serial number and sign-offs belong on one per-unit form. LSN adds a build traveller (Appendix D). Suggest SOP-006 define incoming, in-process and final checks and a per-unit traveller (see also Q23)

kc dislikes the 03_build_package subfolders and asked whether a separate parts.csv is needed. LSN keeps parts.csv and the CSV sources only because tools/check.py and the CAD BOM check read them; people read the generated document. Suggest minimalQMS decide which files are human records and which are machine sources, and flatten the folders

kc: a gate can't approve outputs that don't exist yet. fusion-cad (and SOP-004 G2) had the STEP/STL exports after approval. Make files, BOM and Gerbers must be exported and in the review package before the gate; approval then freezes those versions (milestones after). Also: appendices are separate files (A as CSV for the purchaser, B as a zip of make files), and STL is enough for printed parts

G2 froze software that had never run (LSN lsn-node v0.1.0, written from datasheets). kc: software is not to be frozen at G2. G2 should freeze hardware (what is bought and made); software stays a versioned draft and is released after its tests, by G3

minimalQMS has no way to keep software as its own item: SOP-004 section 9 puts software in the hardware build document (A06, released by G3), so untested software holds up the hardware. kc: "software should be its own thing". Proposal: hardware is verified by a bring-up test plus analysis of capability from datasheets; software is a separate item with its own version, requirements and tests, released on its own; the hardware BOM names the software version only when the product ships with it.

Findings are scattered (review packages, minutes, worklog, chat) with no one place showing what is still open. kc: "you keep spitting this shit out i have no idea where to look for it and whats stll outstanding". Proposal: one findings.csv per product (id, finding, recommendation, decision with the human's words, status) and a gate cannot be asked while any line has no decision.
